use_when: Reserving a square, correctly sized, correctly coloured box for an icon inside another component — the trailing mark in a Button, the leading mark in a Chip.
dont_use_when: As an icon in its own right. `IconSlot` needs no props at all and draws a complete, plausible arrow, so shipping the placeholder is the path of least resistance and nothing stops it — that is the misuse this component invites. Inside Button and Chip the arrow is the default both ship today; anywhere else pass the real icon from Sunim Icon through `icon`, and give it a name when the mark is the only thing carrying the meaning. As a decorative rule or spacer: it is a slot for meaning-bearing or label-adjacent marks, not a spacing device — reach for a margin token or an `<hr>`. As a way to size an icon a parent already sizes: set the parent's own box instead, because this slot is square and will letterbox anything that is not.
placement: Inside another component, next to a text label. It is not laid out directly on a page.
a11y: Two modes, chosen by whether the slot has an accessible name. `label` gives it one and so does `aria-label` — two spellings of one idea, with `label` winning when both are given. Without a name the slot is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`, no role, nothing contributed to the accessibility tree, which is correct beside a label that already says the same thing and is how Button and Chip use it. With a name it becomes `role="img"` carrying that name, and `aria-hidden` is dropped. All three cases verified on the deployed build. `role` and `aria-hidden` stay overridable, because a caller who sets them has a reason this component cannot see. It is never focusable and has no interactive state. Two things it does not guarantee. Contrast: colour is inherited through `--sunim-IconSlot-color` so a caller on a dark or accent surface can retint it without out-specifying its rules, which makes the ratio theirs to meet rather than this component's. And meaning: with no `icon` and no name it renders an arrow that says nothing to anybody, and nothing in the component or the types will tell you.
